data.narrative:
Nomagic is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Kacper Nowicki, Marek Cygan, and Tristan d'Orgeval, having raised $97M to date. The peer universe comprises 3 same-stage, same-sector comparables (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity) alongside a broader landscape of 8 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $97M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying $184M. Peer-median benchmarking references three contemporaneous Series B robotics companies valued between $1.6B and $2.0B, with a median of $1.8B. This reflects the substantial capital deployed into the sector and comparable funding environments.

Triangulation across both methods yields a range of $157M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $967M. The wide spread reflects tension between the conservative stage-progression anchor and the peer-median signal. The $1.8B peer median suggests the broader market has valued robotics companies at substantially higher multiples than the stage-progression method alone implies. Key uncertainties include composition and recency of the peer set, relative maturity and capital efficiency of Nomagic versus named comparables, and whether peer valuations reflect recent downward repricing. A valuation toward the $600M–$1.2B range would balance stage-appropriate conservatism against peer context.
